intro_html: Front end up first, the back end a beat later. An orthopaedic dog bed puts foam that holds its shape under hips and elbows, and many here have a low or open front, so there is nothing to climb.
description_html:
An orthopaedic dog bed earns its name in moments you have probably seen already. The two-stage stand in the morning. The hollow worn into the old bed exactly where the hips go. The stretch that takes a little longer than it used to. Some of it is age. Some of it is a surface that has packed down underneath them, and that part you can change.

What makes an orthopaedic dog bed work

Whether you spell it orthopaedic or orthopedic, the word should mean three physical things. First, foam that does not pack down: every bed in this collection has foam underneath rather than loose fibre (memory foam, profiled egg-crate foam, or memory foam for contour layered over egg-crate for support; Langdale and Patterdale simply list a foam base or core). Second, depth: Ennerdale is 24cm of gel memory foam, and the XXL Mardale and Longsleddale are 20cm deep. Third, a way in that does not ask for a climb. Newlands, Easedale and Burnmoor keep walls on four sides but drop the front section, and Coniston sits low with just a rim for the chin.

Choosing by how they sleep and move

  • If they lean and watch the room: three bolsters and an open front on Grasmere, Melbreak and Rosthwaite, or an L-shaped bolster with two open sides on Esthwaite and Bowfell.
  • If they curl into a corner: Borrowdale has a border on all four sides; Skelwith closes all four around fleece; Helvellyn is a 97 × 97cm triangle that sits flush in the corner beside your sofa.
  • If they stretch flat out: no walls at all on Buttermere (110 × 85cm, 10cm deep), Ambleside (up to 140 × 100cm) or Wastwater (127 × 91cm, with a raised head built into the foam).
  • If they are big and heavy: Mardale, Longsleddale and Burnmoor are 132 × 104cm; Melbreak and Staveley are 122 × 89cm.

Our orthopaedic buying guide takes each of these choices one step further.

Liners, covers and the foam guarantee

One accident can finish an unprotected foam core. Coniston, Borrowdale, Helvellyn, Staveley, Scafell and Newlands, among others, put a waterproof liner between the cover and the foam. Most covers come off to wash; the foam itself never should. Many of the memory foam beds here also carry a 5-year no-flatten guarantee on the foam core, subject to the guarantee terms, and the product page says when a bed does.

A bed is for comfort. It is not a treatment. If your dog is in pain, recovering or finding it hard to move, keep talking to your vet about the right resting surface. If the changes you are seeing have come with age, our beds for older dogs start from there.

Try it for 100 nights

Whether a bed works is something only your dog can tell you, so every orthopaedic dog bed here comes with the 100-night trial from delivery. If they do not settle on it, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund; one trial per household, and damage and other exclusions apply. Standard UK delivery is free on orders over £40. See how the trial works.

Orthopaedic dog bed questions

Will an orthopaedic dog bed help with arthritis?

It cannot treat it, and nothing here should suggest otherwise. What it changes is the surface they lie on for hours every day: foam that spreads their weight instead of bottoming out, and an entry that does not ask for a climb. Your vet is the right person for everything else.

Does an orthopaedic dog bed have to be memory foam?

No. Nocturne, Newlands, Easedale and Burnmoor are built on profiled egg-crate foam, which spreads weight and resists compressing flat. Martindale, Rosthwaite and Watendlath layer memory foam over egg-crate. If it is the moulding feel of memory foam you are after, our memory foam dog beds gather the beds that use it.

What size orthopaedic dog bed do I need?

Take their length lying on their side, nose to base of tail, then add 15 to 20cm. Bolsters sit inside the outside measurement, so if they fall between two sizes, take the bigger one.

Not sure which shape suits them? The Bed Finder starts with how they sleep and narrows it to one bed.
claims_to_confirm: 'Every bed in this collection has foam underneath rather than loose fibre' is true of all 30 members at writing (each description names memory, egg-crate, layered or 'foam core'). The collection is a smart collection (type OR tag 'orthopaedic dog bed'), so a future fibre-filled product with that tag would make the line untrue. Keep the tag for foam beds only.

5-year no-flatten guarantee appears on 20 of the 30 members only (not Langdale, Nocturne, Bowfell, Braithwaite, Burnmoor, Easedale, Esthwaite, Newlands, Patterdale, Scafell). Copy says 'many' and defers to each product page.
Ennerdale's second product image carries on-image text 'CertiPUR-US Certified' and 'Reversible design'. Neither is in the product data. Confirm the certification (with evidence) or replace the image.
Nocturne's fourth product image carries on-image text beginning 'ULTIMATE COMFORT FOR...'. Superlative not supported by the data; consider replacing.
Ambleside's product photos appear to show a rimmed, nest-style bed, while the description says edge-to-edge mattress with 'no soft rim' and 'no walls'. Confirm the photos show the product sold.

Handle/title mismatches worth tidying with redirects: rosthwaite-xl-waterproof-orthopaedic-bed (description mentions no waterproof feature and no dimensions), the-loweswater-orthopaedic-bolster-dog-bed (product is Melbreak), the-kentmere-orthopaedic-bolster-dog-bed (product is Staveley), wasdale-xxl-orthopaedic-sofa-bed (product is Burnmoor).
Burnmoor's description says it needs depth to 'carry 50kg or more without bottoming out'. Not used here; confirm a load rating before repeating it anywhere.

Coniston's first photo appears to show a rectangular, high-sided black-and-cream bed with a third-party label, not the low oval bed its description sets out (and this copy repeats). Confirm the photos show the product sold.
